title: bug: both wrappers route a seat's own role-group/all-tagged chat message back to it as a routed mention, waking it into a notification-only session to answer itself
description: Repro 2026-11-02: worker-33f67e5b's ack msg-0dd03b70 (chan-b6d8273b) quoted the worker role-group tag. The next pre-flight surfaced it as that seat's only routed mention (sender = the seat itself) and spent a fresh notification-only CLI session on a self-reply (msg-33f0eaef). Cause: the mention filters match `worker_id | "all" | role_group` with no `sender == worker_id` skip. Sites: scripts/moe-agent.sh pre-wait probe (~9133-9143) and routed-mention build (~9645-9659); scripts/moe-agent.ps1 :8764 and :9053-9056. The daemon already skips the sender for unread counts (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts:236). Fix: skip messages whose sender is this seat's worker id in all four filters, keep sh/ps1 parity, and add a postflight arm.
definitionOfDone: A message whose sender is the seat's own worker id is neither counted as an unread mention (pre-wait probe) nor listed in <routed_mentions>, in both moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1
Messages from other senders that tag the seat, @all, or its role group still route exactly as before
postflight.{sh,ps1} cover the self-sent case, and parity-check.sh passes

implementationPlan.description:
The sh fix, both filters (DoD 1). scripts/moe-agent.sh is LF; use an editor tool. The exact sender comparison matches the daemon, whose unread counter already skips the sender: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts:236, `targetId !== opts.sender`.
- Pre-wait probe, in the PYEOF heredoc after `targets = {worker_id, "all"}` (~:9140 at 0c44ccf0): change the `hit = ...` line to
  `hit = any(targets & set(m.get("mentions") or []) for m in msgs if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("sender") != worker_id)`
  and add a comment above it: a seat's own message is never its mention (task-ecf78687); the twin is moe-agent.ps1.
- Routed-mention build (~:9648), inside `for msg in extract_msgs(...)`, directly after `if not isinstance(msg, dict): continue`:
  `if msg.get("sender") == worker_id: continue  # own message (task-ecf78687; same in moe-agent.ps1)`
  It sits before the `seen` check and before verified_mention, so a self-sent message is never re-read from the store or counted.

This skips any message the seat sent, whichever tag matched, its own id included. A message with no sender (None) is NOT skipped.

Error handling: both blocks already treat a malformed message as a non-match (the probe's broad except, the build's isinstance guards). msg.get on a dict cannot raise, so no new failure path.

implementationPlan.description:
The ps1 fix, both filters (DoD 1, sh parity). scripts/moe-agent.ps1 starts with a UTF-8 BOM and is LF; keep both. Use an editor tool.
- Pre-wait probe (~:8766 at 0c44ccf0): in `foreach ($msg in @($unread.messages))`, directly after `if (-not $msg -or -not $msg.mentions) { continue }`, add
  `if ([string]$msg.sender -ceq $WorkerId) { continue }  # own message (task-ecf78687; same in moe-agent.sh)`
- Routed-mention build (~:9054): in the bucket loop, directly after `if (-not $msg -or -not $msg.mentions) { continue }`, add the same line.

Why `-ceq` on a `[string]` cast:
- It is exact and ordinal, like the sh `==` and the daemon's `!==`.
- `-eq` would be case-insensitive and would coerce a wire value that is an array or number (mem:gotcha-powershell-eq-coerces-wire-values).
- A missing sender casts to '' and is not skipped.

Error handling: the routed build already sits inside the try that fails closed to MOE_MENTION_EXTRACTION_FAILED, and the probe's cast cannot throw.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: In both wrappers, a chat message whose sender is the seat's own worker id is ignored by the pre-wait unread-mention probe and by the routed-mention build. A seat's own role-group, @all or self-tagged message therefore never skips the wrapper-side task wait, never appears in <routed_mentions>, and never launches a notification-only session. Messages from any other sender that tag the seat, @all or its role group route exactly as before.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Skip sender == workerId in the four wrapper filters, CHOSEN. It matches the daemon's own unread rule (chatStore.ts:236) and needs no daemon or contract change. 2) Make the daemon stop routing a sender's own message. Rejected: chat_read and chat_wait return channel history, not routing, and the wrappers' filters are what treat it as a mention. A daemon change would not fix #general reads. 3) Test only the self case. Rejected: a fix that dropped @all or role-group routing altogether would pass it. The contrast run (FAKE_MENTION=group) pins DoD 2.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Two different signals come from these filters, which is why both pairs of sites matter. The pre-wait probe (sh ~:9131, ps1 ~:8764) decides whether the single-shot wrapper-side task wait runs; its '[no-task] ... waiting up to Ns in the wrapper' line is the observable. The routed-mention build (sh ~:9648, ps1 ~:9054) feeds the routed-mention count, and a taskless launch is skipped only when that count is 0 (sh ~:10087, ps1 ~:9460), which the 'MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=idle' line shows. Both scope helpers run single-shot (--no-loop / -NoLoop, poll interval 0). Scenario AA (:4627 sh) is the no-mention baseline that AB3a must match.

(3) postflight.ps1 runs about 25 minutes, so run it in the background and confirm 'PASS postflight.ps1'. (4) Keep the ps1 BOM.
